entries.title: Whole-quad execution masks in LLVM AMDGPU
entries.title_ru: Маски исполнения пиксельных квадов в LLVM
entries.problem: Handle derivative-related execution while retaining the actual live-lane mask.
entries.similarity: WQM extends the lanes used for derivatives and separately preserves live coverage.
entries.differences: LLVM is a native AMDGPU compiler. XCL emits HLSL/DXIL and the report concerns the destination carry mask.
entries.limits: The pass does not specify XCL's SGPR pair bookkeeping or host compiler behavior.
entries.adaptation: Use the live/expanded distinction as an oracle for mask handling.
entries.test: Compare the carry and adjacent destination with helper pixels at triangle edges in synthetic Wave32 and full-coverage controls.

entries.title: Disjoint lifetime stack colouring in LLVM
entries.title_ru: Переиспользование ячеек по срокам жизни в LLVM
entries.problem: Reduce stack-frame size by reusing stack slots with non-overlapping lifetimes.
entries.similarity: Both allocators need proof that two payloads are never live together.
entries.differences: LLVM colours stack-frame objects. XCL transports per-workgroup GPU payloads between dispatch stages.
entries.limits: The receiver must retain synchronization, alignment and address escape constraints.
entries.adaptation: Adapt the interference rule and conservative fallback, without importing implementation code.
entries.test: Use synthetic crossing and disjoint intervals, branch joins and varying alignment. Compare output hashes and bytes per group.

entries.title: Reject foreign pipeline blobs by device and cache UUID
entries.title_ru: Проверка устройства и UUID кэша в VKD3D-Proton
entries.problem: Detect pipeline blobs incompatible with the current device or Vulkan pipeline cache.
entries.similarity: The header separately identifies device and driver-compatible cache.
entries.differences: VKD3D-Proton validates its own serialized blob. VIctory needs cache file isolation and XCL reports a failure with matching-looking caches.
entries.limits: A matching UUID cannot prove the driver's cached code is safe in the reported configuration.
entries.adaptation: Use validated adapter/cache identity for namespace and a cold fallback for rejected data.
entries.test: Use a tiny public synthetic pipeline with cold/warm driver and application caches in all four combinations, plus a deliberately foreign adapter header.

entries.title: Vulkan pipeline cache header identity
entries.title_ru: Заголовок и идентичность кэша Vulkan
entries.problem: Define the portable header fields for pipeline cache serialization and compatibility.
entries.similarity: The explicit header can serve as an independent check of the candidate cache namespace.
entries.differences: This is the Vulkan contract. It is not an implementation for D3D12 serialized libraries.
entries.limits: Passing header checks is not proof of reuse or absence of driver faults.
entries.adaptation: Check source cache header metadata before reusing library entries and separate diagnostics by adapter.
entries.test: Open a valid cache and a controlled copy with foreign header in a synthetic Vulkan pipeline test.

entries.title: DXVK image barrier batch construction
entries.title_ru: Пакетная сборка барьеров изображений в DXVK
entries.problem: Accumulate image barrier descriptions and issue batched dependency commands.
entries.similarity: Both systems carry old/new layout and affected subresources into a batched submission.
entries.differences: The cited routine batches barrier records. It does not establish Continued's rectangle coalescing rule.
entries.limits: Queue ownership, access masks, aspects and layout differences remain mandatory boundaries.
entries.adaptation: Use the data layout and a non-coalescing reference implementation as a comparison.
entries.test: Replay a synthetic mip/layer grid and compare per-cell transitions, including a hole and mismatched aspects.

entries.title: glibc condition variable broadcast and signal accounting
entries.title_ru: Пробуждение ожидающих потоков в glibc
entries.problem: Wake condition-variable waiters with ordered signal accounting.
entries.similarity: Changes relevant to waiters need a wakeup edge in addition to the shared state change.
entries.differences: glibc implements POSIX condition variables using futexes. Continued uses a C++ condition variable with mode and shutdown predicates.
entries.limits: The library's waiter groups and ordering are not an application-level lock or lifetime protocol.
entries.adaptation: Treat broadcast behavior as a reference and keep the application predicate and lifetime guard.
entries.test: Run a deterministic waiter/mode-switch/shutdown harness with spurious wakes and separate wake-all controls.

entries.title: DXIL StructuredBuffer element stride metadata
entries.title_ru: Размер элемента StructuredBuffer в DXIL
entries.problem: Define resource type metadata used to describe structured-buffer element stride.
entries.similarity: The metadata distinguishes stride from raw byte offsets and supplies a source-backed resource contract.
entries.differences: The compiler document specifies resource metadata rather than a runtime descriptor lookup or console address translation.
entries.limits: One declaration does not reconcile two descriptors with different runtime strides.
entries.adaptation: Use the structure stride contract as a reference for per-descriptor index/remainder conversion.
entries.test: Run a two-descriptor synthetic test at 32 and 56 bytes, checking boundary offsets and the raw buffer control.

entries.title: shadPS4 subgroup lane operations in SPIR-V
entries.title_ru: Операции между линиями подгруппы в shadPS4
entries.problem: Lower console shader lane and quad operations to SPIR-V subgroup operations.
entries.similarity: Both translators need explicit semantics for which host lane supplies a value.
entries.differences: shadPS4 translates PlayStation shaders to SPIR-V; the cited operations stay inside one Vulkan subgroup.
entries.limits: The code does not implement Xbox-style 64 logical lanes on two physical Wave32 subgroups.
entries.adaptation: Reuse its subgroup scoping as a negative boundary and compare any software cross-half design separately.
entries.test: Use distinct values per lane and compare indexes 0, 31, 32 and 63 across native and split Wave sizes.

entries.title: Wine's D3DCompile2 path for legacy HLSL
entries.title_ru: Маршрут компиляции старого HLSL в Wine
entries.problem: Route D3DCompile2 HLSL requests through Wine's compiler backend.
entries.similarity: The open issue compares behavior after switching the old compiler, so the dispatch path is a useful isolation point.
entries.differences: This source shows how the request is compiled. It identifies neither the failing shader nor why the target renders black.
entries.limits: No directly transferable fix is established. DXC DXIL generation does not substitute for the older DXBC contract.
entries.adaptation: Use the compiler entry point to design a diagnostics-only comparison with no driver or title assumptions.
entries.test: Compile the same small public HLSL vertex/pixel pair with identical profile and flags, then compare signatures, diagnostics and draw readback.

entries.title: Vulkan SyncVal negative write-after-write control
entries.title_ru: Отрицательный контроль write-after-write в Vulkan
entries.problem: Verify that an unsafe sequence of render pass and layout transitions triggers a write-after-write diagnostic.
entries.similarity: It supplies a minimal public test for interpreting a WAW diagnostic independent of the vendor runtime.
entries.differences: FrameLab observes the warning inside an NGX recording boundary; the public fixture controls both writers.
entries.limits: The cited test does not expose or repair the closed implementation's command recording.
entries.adaptation: Reuse the methodology to separate an application-controlled hazard from a vendor-owned boundary.
entries.test: Confirm one known WAW positive and one barrier-corrected negative with the same validation layer before comparing the application's public boundary.

entries.title: DXVK adapter LUID reconciliation
entries.title_ru: Сверка LUID видеоадаптеров в DXVK
entries.problem: Reconcile adapter identifiers when reporting DXGI and Vulkan device information.
entries.similarity: Both systems need a stable matching key when friendly device names are ambiguous.
entries.differences: DXVK queries live DXGI/Vulkan properties. victory-fork joins external telemetry samples collected independently.
entries.limits: LUIDs are machine/session context and visibility dependent. Missing validity is not a match.
entries.adaptation: Adapt explicit validity and unknown handling, preserving source names and device identities separately.
entries.test: Test two identical adapter names with distinct LUIDs, one unmatched counter, and a non-valid Vulkan LUID.

entries.title: Vulkan linear local invocation index
entries.title_ru: Линейный индекс локального вызова Vulkan
entries.problem: Define the linear local index for two- and three-dimensional workgroups.
entries.similarity: The specification separates coordinate flattening from subgroup lane position.
entries.differences: The Vulkan local index is a host contract. The receiver must reconstruct console ordering for its own wave layout.
entries.limits: Matching the formula alone does not establish the console subgroup/half mapping.
entries.adaptation: Use the Vulkan index as one input to an explicitly verified mapping rather than aligning an x coordinate to wave size.
entries.test: Emit ID and lane values for 8×8, 16×4 and asymmetric 3D groups and compare the reconstructed sequence to a CPU model.

entries.title: Vulkan queue-family ownership transfer
entries.title_ru: Передача владения ресурсом между очередями Vulkan
entries.problem: Specify matching release/acquire operations for exclusive queue family transitions.
entries.similarity: It establishes the resource lifetime and synchronization contract needed outside the producer queue.
entries.differences: The specification concerns Vulkan queue families. The FrameLab interface also models backend-neutral external completion.
entries.limits: Concurrent sharing, external queue family extensions and timeline semaphore ordering may require different cases.
entries.adaptation: Separate wait/completion and ownership transfer in the synthetic test design.
entries.test: Compare same-family with distinct-family queues, preserve resource contents, and verify a deliberately missing acquire is detected.

entries.title: RPCS3 preserves queue family indices in barrier translation
entries.title_ru: Передача индексов семейств очередей в RPCS3
entries.problem: Translate Vulkan synchronization descriptions while retaining the queue-family fields.
entries.similarity: This shows the importance of carrying ownership metadata when converting synchronization representations.
entries.differences: It is a PS3 RSX host representation and legacy/Vulkan barrier bridge.
entries.limits: It does not implement the destination project's external completion object or importing foreign semaphore handles.
entries.adaptation: Use it as a field-preservation checklist.
entries.test: Run two synthetic queues and compare all barrier ownership and stage fields before and after adaptation.

entries.title: Mesa ACO spill slot assignment
entries.title_ru: Распределение ячеек spill в Mesa ACO
entries.problem: Assign GPU backend spill locations for register pressure and interference.
entries.similarity: It supplies a hardware-grounded comparison for disjoint allocation scopes.
entries.differences: ACO register spilling concerns compiler SSA values and register pressure. XCL scratch payloads can cross dispatches.
entries.limits: Different synchronization domains and spill classes make direct slot equivalence unsafe.
entries.adaptation: Use the separation of slot classes and interference as a design control.
entries.test: Stress different wave widths and spill classes separately from synthetic persistent-dispatch payload tests.

entries.title: RADV shader cache objects
entries.title_ru: Объекты кэша шейдеров RADV
entries.problem: Manage compiled shader/cache objects within the RADV Vulkan driver.
entries.similarity: The boundary helps distinguish a driver cache from an application-level cache.
entries.differences: RADV is a particular Mesa AMD driver, whereas the XCL report names an NVIDIA driver.
entries.limits: Object lifetimes and serialization state in one driver are not portable fixes.
entries.adaptation: Use it to map which cache layer an observation actually refers to.
entries.test: Repeat an open Vulkan pipeline with both cache layers independently enabled or cleared and log driver/UUID.

entries.title: Xenia Vulkan graphics pipeline state cache
entries.title_ru: Кэш графических конвейеров Vulkan в Xenia
entries.problem: Construct and track host Vulkan graphics pipeline objects for Xbox 360 workloads.
entries.similarity: The pipeline key and creation boundary give a historical architecture reference for state caching.
entries.differences: Xbox 360 guest state and Xenia host Vulkan pipeline creation differ from Xbox Series D3D12 pipeline libraries.
entries.limits: It is not a serialized driver-blob or adapter migration solution.
entries.adaptation: Compare which bits of state are needed for a deterministic descriptor and variant key.
entries.test: Use two synthetic descriptors differing in one graphics state and check separate host pipeline reuse without cache collisions.

entries.title: VMA virtual allocation and linear suballocation
entries.title_ru: Виртуальное распределение памяти в VMA
entries.problem: Allocate and free offsets within a virtual block without allocating actual Vulkan device memory.
entries.similarity: It is a useful test reference for alignment, bounds and allocation strategy.
entries.differences: A virtual block tracks offsets but does not prove two GPU users are disjoint in time.
entries.limits: Explicit ownership and synchronization are caller responsibilities.
entries.adaptation: Use the allocator's offset checks as a control for a separately validated lifetime algorithm.
entries.test: Test aligned offsets, wraparound, exhaustion and two active ranges that must remain disjoint.

entries.title: D3D12MA virtual blocks and aliased allocation
entries.title_ru: Виртуальные блоки и алиасинг в D3D12MA
entries.problem: Describe the allocation and resource primitives used when multiple resources occupy memory in one heap.
entries.similarity: The resource placement boundary makes the difference between shared backing memory and active resource correctness explicit.
entries.differences: It allocates offsets/resources on a host heap. It does not know a console shader's execution lifetime.
entries.limits: Aliasing barriers, alignment, resource flags and lifetime proof are separate constraints.
entries.adaptation: Use documented constraints when designing a focused host allocation test.
entries.test: Compare two placed-resource alias intervals with explicit barriers plus a negative test using overlapping active lifetimes.

entries.title: SPIRV-Tools access-chain validation
entries.title_ru: Валидация цепочки доступа в SPIRV-Tools
entries.problem: Validate pointer access through a SPIR-V aggregate and its index operands.
entries.similarity: The validator provides a checked structural baseline for tests of generated code.
entries.differences: SPIR-V aggregate type validation is different from D3D12 descriptor stride and does not run the target's shader.
entries.limits: A structurally valid module can still access the wrong logical element.
entries.adaptation: Use the validator before comparing real readback, while keeping the runtime result as a separate check.
entries.test: Generate a small valid module and a wrong index-type module, then independently check actual buffer element selection.

entries.title: Closed wgpu proposal for acceleration-structure scratch reuse
entries.title_ru: Закрытое предложение wgpu по временному буферу ускоряющих структур
entries.problem: Reduce repeated scratch buffer allocation during acceleration structure builds.
entries.similarity: It addresses reuse of a temporary GPU allocation.
entries.differences: An acceleration-structure builder scratch buffer is distinct from shader payload lifetime slots.
entries.limits: PR closed without merge. The recorded PR head is evidence of a proposal only.
entries.adaptation: Use as a rejected transfer case for XCL scratch slots and compare separate allocator costs only where acceleration structures are actually used.
entries.test: Vary scratch sizes across repeated synthetic builds and compare resource counts without attributing shader spill behavior.

entries.title: MoltenVK proposal to size tessellation scratch from reflection
entries.title_ru: Предложение MoltenVK о размере памяти тесселяции по отражению шейдера
entries.problem: Propose deriving tessellation intermediate sizes from actual shader output reflection.
entries.similarity: Both cases are about reducing oversized temporary allocations.
entries.differences: The patch concerns tessellation stage output on Metal rather than dispatch-to-dispatch lifetimes on D3D12.
entries.limits: The examined proposal is open. No merge or receiver applicability has been established.
entries.adaptation: Use it as an example of independent reflection-based sizing, keeping the lifetime problem separate.
entries.test: Construct two synthetic shaders with different reflected output sizes and compare required buffer sizes and results.

entries.title: Closed SyncVal WAW report with secondary command buffers
entries.title_ru: Закрытый отчёт SyncVal о двойной записи во вторичных буферах
entries.problem: Explain a WAW diagnostic when a multisubpass render pass uses secondary command buffers.
entries.similarity: Both reports need to distinguish an actual output hazard from how SyncVal records commands.
entries.differences: The archived report describes SDK 1.3.280.0 and a secondary command buffer. The FrameLab report is at the NGX boundary.
entries.limits: The pinned SDK is the code reference for the reported version. Closure and reviewer discussion do not establish a fix for FrameLab.
entries.adaptation: Use the secondary buffer vs inline command contrast as a separate diagnostics control.
entries.test: Run both library-independent variants with the same layers and compare IDs and actual attachment output.

entries.title: Vice-Tay DXIL regression for separate buffer size and load handles on RDNA4
entries.title_ru: Тест Vice-Tay на раздельное чтение размера и данных буфера в DXIL
entries.problem: Check that distinct handles for a buffer size query and a load survive DXIL optimization.
entries.similarity: VIctory #2122 separates size queries from loads. Vice-Tay asserts the operands stay separate with a view index limit.
entries.differences: Vice-Tay also prevents reuse of certain size queries and clamps. The VIctory hardware fixture covers a raw buffer.
entries.limits: The AMD results cover Vice-Tay at the reported revisions and driver. The proposed control is untested on the VIctory branch.
entries.adaptation: Adapt the emitted DXIL assertions to a structured buffer alongside the raw-buffer hardware check.
entries.test: Toggle the heap clamp and compare handles and clamp operands after optimization. Report AMD and WARP hardware checks separately.

entries.title: VIctory Agility SDK smoke test for D3D12 heap-indexed root signatures
entries.title_ru: Проверка Agility SDK для прямой индексации дескрипторов D3D12
entries.problem: A Windows 10 root signature with direct heap indexing is refused before any draws reach the host.
entries.similarity: VIctory #3618 and AnyXboxX #559 report the same OS build and root signature flag refusal on different adapters. VIctory #969 tests that exact flag combination through the configured runtime.
entries.differences: VIctory #969 uses an Agility device factory. The app-local export route in VIctory #463 was validated separately. AnyXboxX has its own vendored runtime.
entries.limits: The test proves creation of an empty 0xC01 root signature. The current head is open. It leaves game startup, frame rendering, and Vega 8 compatibility unverified.
entries.adaptation: Compare the configured runtime with the system-runtime result before investigating later crashes. Use the Microsoft package matching the selected candidate.
entries.test: Set VICTORY_D3D12_AGILITY to the folder containing the official x64 D3D12Core.dll. Run cargo test -p victory-shader --release creates_device_and_serializes_heap_indexed_root_signature_when_configured. Without the variable the test returns early.

cases.title: HLSL pixel masks: adjacent Wave32 carry destinations lose s21 on WQM triangle edges
cases.conclusion: Use live versus expanded mask as an oracle.

cases.title: Recompiler: reuse scratch slots across disjoint payload lifetimes
cases.conclusion: Apply interference checks to the separate inter-dispatch allocation policy.

cases.title: Linux / NVIDIA: XCL's cached driver blob plus a warm NVIDIA shader cache crashes in vkCreateGraphicsPipelines
cases.query: Vulkan pipeline cache UUID driver blob
cases.conclusion: Compare both cache layers with separate toggles. The crash cause is open.

cases.title: vulkan: coalesce equal image layout ranges (VK-IMAGE-LAYOUT-RANGE-COALESCING)
cases.query: Vulkan image layout barrier range coalescing
cases.conclusion: Use the non-coalescing batch as a reference. Rule equivalence needs testing.

cases.title: frame_pacer: wake blocked waiters on set_uncapped and guard shutdown entry
cases.conclusion: Compare awakened and sleeping paths, keeping predicates in the receiver.

cases.title: Shaders: split flat byte-offset accesses to structured buffers
cases.conclusion: Use stride metadata as the oracle for two descriptors.

cases.title: GPU: one host pipeline library for every adapter, so a WARP run discards the hardware one
cases.conclusion: Use per-adapter keying and retain foreign-cache rejection.

cases.title: VIctory on NVIDIA (32-lane waves): 17 wave64 compute pipelines refused per run on main (RTX 5080)
cases.conclusion: Use subgroup scoping. Cross-half software work remains separate.

cases.title: Neptune base on Linux (Wine, RTX 5060 8 GB): black with Wine's d3dcompiler; with Microsoft's, Series X draws at ~0.2 fps and Series S is grey at ~1.2 fps
cases.conclusion: No transferable compiler fix found in the bounded scan. Suggested test isolates legacy code and signatures.

cases.title: Investigate Vulkan SyncVal WAW diagnostics inside the NGX recording boundary
cases.conclusion: No direct vendor-side implementation found. Start with a published positive/negative pair.

cases.title: Resource collector: GPU counter LUIDs cannot be matched to adapter names in multi-GPU captures
cases.conclusion: Separate unknown identifiers and validation of real matches.

cases.title: Console thread ids in 2-D/3-D compute groups on 32-lane hosts: the wave-aligned rounding in `thread_id` / `console_thread` does not hold (RTX 4060 Laptop, Radeon 780M)
cases.conclusion: Do not substitute local index for subgroup lane. Compare mappings on asymmetric groups.

cases.title: Validate external completion and multi-queue resource handoff
cases.query: Vulkan queue family ownership release acquire
cases.conclusion: Use contract and field-preservation reference on two controlled queues.

cases.title: Check a buffer size query and a load after DXIL optimization
cases.conclusion: Use the Vice-Tay DXIL test as a template for the structured-buffer follow-up. Applicability remains to be tested on VIctory.

cases.title: Diagnose rejected direct heap indexing on Windows 10
cases.conclusion: Run the pinned test on the reported Vega 8. Track the root-signature refusal with the Agility work if it passes.

cases.title: Diagnose rejected direct heap indexing on Windows 10
cases.conclusion: Use this as a historical comparison. The issue was closed with a diagnosis and the receiving branch still needs a check.
